title: Law student David Fuchs promoted to first lieutenant at Pepperdine ceremony
text:
Law student David Fuchs promoted to first lieutenant at Pepperdine ceremony
Pepperdine Caruso School of Law student David Fuchs was promoted to first lieutenant in the United States Marine Corps during a ceremony held on Aug. 10 at the university’s DiLoreto Patio. The event marked a significant milestone for Fuchs as he continues his path toward becoming a judge advocate general, serving as both lawyer and legal advisor in the armed forces.
Fuchs was surrounded by friends, military colleagues, faculty mentors, and family as 1stLt Christopher Impellizzeri, officer selection officer in the Marine Corps, administered the military Oath of Office. After taking the oath, Fuchs received his new silver bar insignia to signify his promotion from second lieutenant.
“I’ve been a Marine throughout my whole time at Pepperdine and now I have the privilege of being promoted here,” Fuchs said. “It is an honor and a privilege to take the next step toward leadership in the United States Marines. Years ago I took that as a call and responded.”
Fuchs began studying law just one week after his initial commission on August 10, 2024. Now entering his third year at Caruso School of Law with plans to graduate in spring 2027, he credited Arnold Barba—Marine Corps veteran and associate dean for professional development—with guiding him into “the lawyer, man, and marine I was called to be.” Barba attended the ceremony and participated in changing Fuchs’s officer rank insignia pins.
The incoming JD class of 2029 also attended as part of their launch week activities. Barba said about Fuchs, “David always understood the gravity of what he is here to do... He always displayed a desire to be formed into a leader that can carry the weight and importance that they’re assigned in their field.”
After graduation and passing the bar exam, Fuchs intends to return to active duty as a Marine Corps Judge Advocate. In this role he will serve both as an attorney and commissioned officer—a dual responsibility distinct within military branches due to rigorous training requirements for unrestricted line officers before assuming legal duties.
Eric Leshinsky, director of student veteran affairs at Pepperdine University and retired Air Force colonel who attended the event, said: “Pinning on his first lieutenant bars is a significant milestone for David... It gives students an opportunity to see a person considering service, and they may follow in his footsteps.”
Pepperdine University supports more than 500 enrolled veterans, service members, ROTC cadets, and their dependents.
